info.title: OpenBot API
info.description: Headless REST API for OpenBot. To authenticate, send `Authorization: Bearer <user token>`. Create tokens at /v1/user/tokens. Every call needs a permission from a role or policy. Browser clients on the same origin can use the sign-in session Cookie instead. Then every write must send the exact public Origin.

post.description: Sends a message to your Chat with this Bot. OpenBot makes the Chat the first time. When the Bot is free, the message starts a Turn at once. When the Bot works for you, it reads the message at its next step. You need `bots.delegate` on the Bot.

post.description: Sends a message to a direct Chat, a task Chat or a live Chat. In a task Chat, the Bot reads it as a message from you. In a live Chat, the message waits until a Live session is open.

get.description: Lists your Chats. Without `kind`, it lists direct Chats, channel Chats and live Chats.
Returns the Chat, its current Turn and its latest response. Reading never starts work.

patch.description: Changes the mode, the model or the plan approval of the Chat. A new model also needs `models.use`.

delete.description: Deletes the history of a direct Chat, a channel Chat or a live Chat. It stops the running Turn and cancels the work that the Chat gave away first. The next message starts an empty Chat.

get.description: Lists the Items of the Chat, newest first. Send `next` as `before` to read older Items.

post.description: Stops the running Turn. The work that the Chat gave to Bots goes on, unless `delegations` is true.

put.description: Replaces the todo list of the Chat. The Bot also changes it with its todo tool.

Lists what the Bot said with `confide` in this Chat, and the answers that it got. The Bot uses it to talk about how its work goes. See the client guide before you show it to people.
Lists what the memory Bot added to the input of each Turn, and the Bot memory entries that it used.

post.description: Makes a new live Chat of yours with this Bot. Then open its Live WebSocket. You need `bots.delegate` on the Bot and `models.use` on the Live model.

get.description: Opens the Live WebSocket of a live Chat. Each thing the person says starts a Turn, and the Bot answers with sound and text. Turns use the shared execution engine. Sound stays on the open connection. A browser must connect from the public origin.

post.description: Uploads one file through OpenBot, as `multipart/form-data` with the field `file`. The file is ready at once. The platform can turn this way off.

get.description: Lists the files that you may read, newest first.

post.description: Makes a pending file and a signed address in object storage. The client puts the bytes there itself, then completes the file. The platform can turn this way off.
Checks that the bytes are in object storage with the right size, and makes the file ready.

delete.description: Deletes a file now. Chats that used it keep their text, but the model no longer sees the file.

get.description: Gives the bytes of a ready file.

category.description: What a client can do next: invalid (change the input), forbidden, not_found, conflict (read again), limited (a limit or budget stopped the work; try again after it changes), unavailable (try again later), external, outcome_unknown, interrupted.

get.description: Reads one piece of work that a Bot gave away, from one of your Chats.

post.description: Asks the execution to stop this work and its child work. Observe the execution until its resources are released.

get.description: Lists the Bots that the caller can use: their own Bots and the shared Bots. With `bot`, it lists the Bots that this Bot owns.

Reads the entries of the Bot memory that the caller may see: entries for the caller, for a Channel group that the caller is in, or for everyone who uses the Bot, in the organization of the caller. Nobody can read the memory about another person.

post.description: Remembers something about the caller, or takes back what the caller gave to an entry.

get.description: Lists the changes that touch entries that the caller may see.

post.description: Removes every entry with one tag of OpenBot, like `from:<userId>` or `chat:<id>`, without showing them. It needs `bots.write` on a Bot that is not linked.

get.description: Reads the settings of the memory Bot that keeps the memory of this Bot. It needs `bots.write` on a Bot that is not linked.

patch.description: Changes the rules, the concurrency and the budget of the memory Bot. It needs `bots.write` on a Bot that is not linked.

post.description: Adds a Rule that the caller wrote for this Bot. A Rule from a person is active at once.

patch.description: Changes the text of a Rule, confirms a proposed Rule, or retires a Rule.

delete.description: Revokes a Grant and every Grant that came from it.

get.description: Lists the people who use this Bot in their own organizations. It needs `bots.share`.

delete.description: Takes a person off this Bot. Their linked Bot stops working at once.

post.description: Invites a person by email, or makes an invitation link, to use this Bot. It needs `bots.share`. Only a lasting top Bot can be shared. Email invitations return the mail delivery status when created. A failed send does not remove the invitation.

get.description: Reads the secret and the URL of an invitation link again, for example to print its QR code again.

post.description: Sends a pending email invitation again. It needs `bots.share`. The end time stays the same. Link invitations cannot be sent by email.

delete.description: Takes back a pending invitation. People who accepted it stay members.

post.description: Accepts an email invitation (`invitation`) or an invitation link (`secret`). It makes a linked Bot in your organization and gives it back. When you already use the Bot, it gives back your linked Bot.

get.description: Lists the requests that wait for the caller, or that the caller answered.

post.description: Saves one decision and returns its execution receipt. The workflow sends the result to the Chat.

patch.description: Changes your settings. Send the `version` that you read as `expectedVersion`. If they changed since then, the change fails with SettingsConflict.

get.description: Lists the triggers that the caller can read: their own and the shared ones.

patch.description: Changes a trigger. The caller becomes its actor, so the new tasks work for the caller.

put.description: Makes a new webhook secret. The old secret stops working. The caller becomes the actor of the trigger.

post.description: Gives the task of the trigger to its Bot. Send `Authorization: Bearer <webhook secret>`. The JSON body goes to the Bot as data, not as instructions. The task works for the actor of the trigger.
Saves a Channel and starts its configuration execution. The caller becomes its actor. Read executionId to check registration.

patch.description: Changes a Channel. The caller becomes its actor.

delete.description: Stops Channel work, then deletes the Channel and its links. Read the returned execution to wait for release. Its Chats stay.

put.description: Makes a new signing secret for a custom Channel. The old secret stops working.

delete.description: Unlinks a person. The bot asks them to link again.

get.description: Shows who a link code is for, so the person can check it before they accept.

post.description: Links the person on the platform to the caller. A code works only once.

Takes an event from Slack, Lark, Telegram or a custom Channel. OpenBot checks the signature, answers at once, and does the work later. A custom Channel sends a `CustomEvent` with `X-OpenBot-Timestamp` and `X-OpenBot-Signature: sha256=<hex HMAC-SHA256 of timestamp + "." + body>`.

get.description: Lists the Computer providers that the caller can use: their own and the shared ones.

post.description: Adds an account at a Computer provider. OpenBot checks the key with the provider first.

delete.description: Deletes a Computer provider. It fails while Computers still use it.

get.description: Lists the Computers that the caller can use: their own and the shared ones. With `bot`, it lists only the Computers that this Bot has the right to use.

post.description: Accepts a command to create a Computer and returns its execution receipt. Reuse the command key after a lost reply. A connector Computer stays offline until it connects.

404.description: ComputerNotFound | ComputerPathNotFound | ComputerSessionNotFound | ComputerProviderNotFound | PairingInvalid | ExecutionNotFound

delete.description: Accepts a command to delete a Computer and its sandbox, files and Bot grants. Follow its execution receipt for the result. A lost provider reply waits for a decision.

get.description: Lists the Bots that have the right to use a Computer.

put.description: Gives a Bot the right to use a Computer. The caller must be able to use the Computer and to change the Bot.

delete.description: Takes the right to use a Computer away from a Bot. The Computer stays.

get.description: Lists the times when a Computer ran, newest first. The provider bills them. OpenBot only records them.

put.description: Makes a new token for the connector of a connector Computer. The old token stops working, and its connection closes.

post.description: Starts a shell command and waits up to yieldTimeMs for it. When it still runs, the answer has a session ID for more input and output. A paused Computer resumes first.
Sends text to the stdin of a session, and gives the output since the last call.

delete.description: Stops the command of a session, and gives its last output.

put.description: Writes a file. OpenBot makes the missing directories.

delete.description: Removes a file, or a directory with everything in it.

put.description: Gives a port a public HTTPS address.

post.description: Does the actions in order, then takes a screenshot.
Gives an address where a person can watch and use the desktop.

get.description: Shows which machine a pairing code is for, so the person can check it before they approve.

post.description: Approves a machine. OpenBot creates a connector Computer for it, and the machine gets its token on its next poll. The Computer belongs to the caller, or to the organization when `shared` is true. When the same machine pairs again, OpenBot keeps its Computer and only changes the token. Only a person can approve.
Denies a machine. Its pairing ends at once.
Starts a pairing for a machine. The code works for 10 minutes.
Tells the machine if a person approved it. Send `Authorization: Bearer <secret>` with the secret of the pairing.

get.description: Lists the secret providers that the caller can use: their own and the shared ones.

post.description: Adds an account at a secret provider. OpenBot checks the token with the provider first.

delete.description: Deletes a secret provider. It fails while Vault items still read from it.

get.description: Lists the Vaults that the caller can use: their own and the shared ones.

delete.description: Deletes a Vault, its items and the rights of all Bots to use it. The secret providers keep their secrets.

post.description: Adds an item. For an item of a secret provider, the caller must be able to use the provider, and OpenBot reads the item once to check that its fields are there.

get.description: Lists the Bots that have the right to use a Vault.

put.description: Gives a Bot the right to use every item of a Vault in Code Mode. The caller must be able to use the Vault and to change the Bot.

delete.description: Takes the right to use a Vault away from a Bot.

get.description: Adds up the tokens and the cost of the model calls in a time range. `groupBy` is `day` when you leave it out.
Lists model calls, the newest first. Send `next` as `after` to get the next page.

post.description: Adds a budget. Each scope can have one budget for each period.

get.description: Lists the organizations where you are a member. A user token sees only its own organization.

post.description: Creates an organization. You become its Super Administrator. The platform settings say who can do this.

delete.description: Leaves an organization. Your tokens in it stop working. The last active Super Administrator cannot leave. A user token can only leave its own organization.

get.description: Lists the pending invitations for your verified email.

post.description: Joins the organization of the invitation. You need the session cookie, and your verified email must be the email of the invitation. An invitation to use a Bot needs `POST /v1/bot-invitations/accept` instead.
Says no to an invitation. You need the session cookie and the email of the invitation.

Sends a test email with the current platform SMTP settings. Only platform admins can use this endpoint. Sent means that SMTP accepted the email; it does not prove inbox delivery. A failed send is not retried.

Suspends an organization or makes it active again. Nobody can use a suspended organization, and its tokens stop working.

get.description: Lists the current price of each model of a provider of the platform. Organizations pay this price with their credits.

503.description: PlatformUnavailable | OrganizationStorageUnavailable | ModelProviderOAuthUnavailable | ModelProvidersUnavailable | AuthenticationUnavailable | RequestFailed | FeatureUnavailable

put.description: Sets a new price for one model of the provider. The price applies to calls from now on. Old calls keep their cost.

patch.description: Turns the credits of an organization on or off. While they are on, the organization can use the models of the platform only when its balance is more than 0.

post.description: Adds credits to an organization. A negative amount takes credits back.

get.description: Shows who the caller is and, for a token, its policy. Every caller can use it.

patch.description: Changes the status, roles or extra policy of a member. A suspended member cannot sign in, and their tokens stop working.

delete.description: Removes a member and revokes their tokens. If their email domain is still allowed, they join again the next time they sign in. Suspend them to keep them out.

get.description: Lists the invitations of the organization, newest first.

post.description: Invites a person by email. They accept with `POST /v1/invitations/:invitationId/accept` after they sign in with that verified email. An invitation lasts 7 days. When mail is set up, OpenBot sends it and returns the delivery status. A failed send does not remove the invitation.
Sends a pending email invitation again. Its roles and end time stay the same. Only a Super Administrator can send an invitation with that role.

patch.description: Changes the settings. Send the `version` that you read as `expectedVersion`. If someone changed the settings since then, the change fails with SettingsConflict. Every instance uses the new settings right away.

get.description: Lists the built-in roles and the custom roles of the organization.

post.description: Creates a custom role. Its policy cannot allow anything that you cannot do yourself.

patch.description: Changes a custom role. Every member with the role gets the new policy at once.

delete.description: Deletes a custom role. It fails with RoleInUse while a member or the default roles use it.

get.description: Lists audit log entries, newest first. `actor` filters by user ID.
Lists the models that the caller may use now, for each provider that offers them.
Lists the models of the organization. The models that the platform shares are not in the list.

post.description: Adds a model to the organization. Link it to a provider to use it.
Adds a model provider. ChatGPT uses sign-in; other kinds need an API key.

patch.description: Changes a model provider. The next model call uses the change.

get.description: Lists the current price of each model of a provider of the organization. Usage of these models counts toward budgets, but never takes credits.

put.description: Sets a new price for one model of the provider. The price applies to calls from now on. Old calls keep their cost.

post.description: Adds an email domain. Then add the TXT record that the answer names, and call the verify endpoint.
Looks up the TXT record of the domain. When it is right, the domain becomes verified.
Adds an OpenID Connect provider for people with an email in verified domains of the organization.

get.description: Shows where to find the API reference, the Better Auth routes and the user token routes.
Checks that the HTTP service can respond. It does not check business dependencies.
